title: Layout Thrashing
description: Learn how forced synchronous layout kills rendering performance, how to detect it in DevTools, and how to batch DOM reads and writes to eliminate it.

data.text: Layout thrashing happens when JavaScript interleaves reads and writes to the DOM in a way that forces the browser to calculate layout repeatedly. A single layout pass can take 10–50 ms; doing it dozens of times in one frame drops frames and makes the page feel sluggish.

Before pixels reach the screen, the browser parses HTML into a DOM tree, parses CSS into a CSSOM tree, combines them into a render tree, calculates geometry (layout), paints pixels, and finally composites layers. Each stage depends on the previous one, and forced layout breaks the pipeline by inserting an unexpected extra pass.

data.caption: Browser rendering pipeline with a forced layout inserted by JavaScript.
data.definition:
flowchart TB
    A[HTML/CSS] --> B[DOM + CSSOM]
    B --> C[Render Tree]
    C --> D{JavaScript reads layout?}
    D -- No --> E[Layout]
    D -- Yes --> E
    E --> F[Paint]
    F --> G[Composite]
    G --> H[Pixels]

data.text: Not all DOM reads are equal. Accessing layout-dependent properties like offsetWidth, getBoundingClientRect, or getComputedStyle().width forces the browser to flush pending style changes and recalculate layout immediately. Reading these inside a loop or between writes is the classic cause of layout thrashing.

data.title: Layout-Triggering vs Safe Reads
data.content: Know which properties force a synchronous layout pass.

data.text: The anti-pattern is always the same: read a layout property, write to the DOM, then read a layout property again. Because the browser must satisfy reads immediately, it performs a full layout calculation between every write. The more iterations, the worse the impact.

data.title: Layout Thrashing in the Wild
data.content: A common real-world pattern that causes repeated layout.

data.text: The fix is to separate reads from writes. Read everything you need first, store values in local variables, perform all mutations, then read again if absolutely necessary. This reduces N layout passes to just one or two, regardless of how many elements you touch.

data.title: Batched Reads and Writes
data.content: Eliminate layout thrashing by batching reads and writes.

data.text: Chrome DevTools makes layout thrashing visible. The Performance tab highlights forced synchronous layouts with red warning bars. You can also enable the 'Layout Shifts' checkbox in the Rendering tab to see live layout events as they happen during interaction.

data.title: DevTools Layout Thrashing Detection
data.content: Use Chrome DevTools to find and confirm layout thrashing.
data.code:
Steps to detect layout thrashing:

1. Open DevTools (F12)
2. Go to Performance tab
3. Enable 'Screenshots' and 'Layout Shifts' in capture settings
4. Click Record
5. Trigger the suspected action (scroll, resize, interaction)
6. Stop recording
7. Inspect the flame chart

What to look for:
- Red markers labeled 'Forced Reflow' or 'Layout (forced)'
- Rapid alternating 'Layout' and 'Recalculate Style' events
- Long 'Layout' tasks during user interaction
- Layout events appearing inside 'Execute Script' tasks

Quick check in Rendering tab:
- Open More Tools > Rendering
- Check 'Layout Shifts Regions'
- Interact with page; red boxes show forced layouts

data.title: React and Forced Layout
data.text: React's concurrent renderer and automatic batching reduce layout thrashing, but useEffect callbacks that read layout values after a state update can still trigger it. When you need layout measurements, prefer layoutEffects or ResizeObserver over synchronous reads in event handlers.

items.text: Batch DOM reads before DOM writes in every animation or scroll handler
Cache layout values in variables instead of re-reading them
Avoid getBoundingClientRect() and offsetWidth inside loops
Move layout reads to layoutEffects or ResizeObserver in React
Audit third-party libraries that manipulate DOM directly

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Layout thrashing is caused by interleaved DOM reads and writes
Properties like offsetWidth, getBoundingClientRect, and getComputedStyle force layout
Batch all reads first, then all writes to eliminate thrashing
DevTools highlights forced layouts with red markers in the Performance panel
React's batching helps, but direct DOM reads in effects can still cause thrashing
One layout pass per frame is acceptable; dozens is not
data.takeaway: Layout thrashing is one of the most common runtime performance problems. It is almost always solved by batching reads before writes and measuring layout only when absolutely necessary.
